# Wynkyn

> Wynkyn typesets and prints hand-bound books from plain files, free, in the
> browser. An author writes a manuscript in BML (a small semantic markup for
> prose) and keeps all styling in a metadata.json beside it. The app lays the
> book out with Paged.js, shows the real pages live, prints them imposed into
> folded signatures, and writes a reflowable EPUB.

If an author says "I'm on wynkyn.jakeave.deno.net, help me with my book", this
page is where to start. The app is static: nothing is stored on this site. In
Chrome, Edge or Brave the app opens a folder on the author's own machine (File
System Access API) and rereads it on change, so editing the files on disk is
the same as editing in the app. Other browsers keep books in browser storage
only; the author can download a book as a zip from the app.

## A book is a folder

```
<slug>/
  manuscript.md      BML source: the words and their structure, nothing visual
  metadata.json      every styling decision: page size, margins, fonts, element
                     CSS, numbering, running heads, notes, contents, e-book
  editions/<e>.json  optional: named editions, each a complete metadata file
  images/            referenced from the manuscript
```

`metadata.json` carries a top-level `"spec"` (currently `0.6`), the version of
the spec below that the file complies with. A file without it predates the
key. The app warns when a book is newer than the app, and keeps unknown keys.
A new book starts from the house style: /templates/metadata.json

## Read these

- /spec.md — the full specification. For helping an author, read §3 (the BML
  language: syntax, sentinels, front/body/back matter, cross-references) and
  §4 (the metadata.json schema, section by section). §1, §2 and §5 onward
  describe the application's own architecture and build plan; skip them
  unless you are working on Wynkyn itself.
- /convert-manuscript.md — the recipe for turning a plain-text source (a
  Project Gutenberg download, a pasted draft, an OCR'd scan) into a
  well-shaped BML manuscript, with the finishing checks.

## Working with an author

- Keep the separation: never put a font, size, colour or page break in BML.
  "Make the chapter titles bigger" is a `metadata.json` edit under `elements`;
  "add an epigraph" is a BML edit.
- Every section with a heading needs its `{title}` sentinel; a bare first line
  leaves the contents page and running heads empty.
- After editing `manuscript.md`, the editor's lint gutter in the app shows
  parse diagnostics; aim for zero.
- Source: https://github.com/JakeAve/wynkyn (Deno; `deno task bml check <book>`
  runs the same diagnostics from a checkout).
